title: First trombone jobs and the Gabriel family
summary: Humphrey recalls his first jobs, Manny Gabriel hiring him, and the Gabriel family connections.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: After I started on trombone. That fella named Portris Market Dan, a guitar player. Mm-hmm. First job I went on. He played guitar. Went out Spanish for the West End or somewhere else. Played that job. Next son, he had another job. I went out there and trade. Well, I'm getting a little better and better all the time, see. Well, Those, uh, pavilions used to be, you know, just jammed up, you know, just about, say about 20 feet apart. Mm-hmm. Out there, you know.
Old time, long time, of course. Mm-hmm.

Manny, uh, Manny Gabriel. He heard me play. He had a weekend, you know, weekend job. Even him. Oh, good, wow. He's pretty nice trumpet player. Him and Duke Gabriel and his son played drums. Little Manny. What did Gabriel play now? The guitar. You know Gabriel played guitar.
Yeah, man. What, uh, you met?
I never have met him, I don't think.
Yeah, Clarence. I know his brother, Percy. He's a little better fella.
I know Percy, the one that played the bass, but he's awful young. I doubt if you knew him. What did you know him?
Well, uh, August married one of, uh, uh, uh, uh, Miss Gabriel's daughter. You know August, the bass player?
Yeah, August Lanois. Well, he married, uh, one of, uh, I don't know. Yeah, he had, had, had two dollars, I know.
